acceptance: An upstream Theseus issue or change exists for retrying idempotent GitHub reads on 5xx in the prepare step, and is linked here.
BenchBox pins a Theseus version in which a single 503 on the pull-request read does not fail the review job, or the owner records a decision not to change it.
The recovery command for a review that died before any reviewer ran is stated in `docs/agent/merge-authority.md` next to the sentence that tells agents to re-run a review when a reviewer errors.

Delivery shape: one upstream Theseus change covers this item and theseus-gate-transient-github-timeout-20261113 if the source check confirms both reads can share the retry in `theseus_reviewer/github.py`; then one BenchBox PR bumps the Theseus lock (own PR, never in a batch). Verification rubric: pass = (1) the source finding (retry path missing for this read, or 503 outlasted it) recorded with file and function at the pinned version; (2) an upstream test injects one 503 then success on the pull-request read in prepare and the job proceeds, and injects persistent 503 and the job fails with a message naming the read; (3) no retry wraps any POST of a verdict, status or comment (test asserts call count 1 on a failing post); (4) BenchBox lock bump merged and one real review job on that pin completes; (5) merge-authority.md states the re-dispatch command. Fail = a stand-in approval or relaxed gate used as recovery, a retried write, or the lock bump inside a batch. Decision recorded by owner on the rerun-budget question, or explicitly deferred with a reason. Base guardrails: Theseus work in a Theseus worktree under its own review; BenchBox work in a linked worktree; no live-cloud spend.

Owner decision 2026-11-17: in scope this round, fixed once upstream in Theseus together with theseus-gate-transient-github-timeout-20261113, then a separate BenchBox lock-bump PR. A review job that fails in 'Prepare the review' does not count against the daily rerun budget, because no reviewer ran.

2026-11-17: upstream fix merged as joeharris76/theseus#91 (aa4dd53). Source finding: `theseus_reviewer/github.py` had no read retry at all (`from .retry import State` is the review-attempt state, not a network retry), so one 503 in `_gh_bytes` failed the prepare step; the gate's urllib reads (`review_check._request`, `fetch_text`, `fetch_optional_bytes`) had none either. The fix retries reads only (3 attempts, 2 s then 5 s) on 5xx and network timeouts/resets; `gh api` calls with write flags and GraphQL mutations run once, and an unrecognised GraphQL call is treated as a write. The gate error status now keeps the endpoint path. Reviewed by three independent fresh-context reviews (SHIP on 2b3e6da, bba15b7, e48746f) and the hosted review (SHIP after D1-D3 fixed). Owner authorized cutting the release; another session had already opened theseus#93 'Prepare release 0.2.14' and merged main (including #91) into it, so the release is left to that PR. Remaining here: BenchBox lock bump to v0.2.14 on its own PR, plus the re-dispatch command in docs/agent/merge-authority.md.

2026-11-18: recovery line merged in BenchBox #4347 (docs/agent/merge-authority.md, next to 're-run it when a reviewer errors'): `gh workflow run review-verdict.yml --ref develop -f pr=<number> -f head=<head SHA>`, and that a failure before any reviewer ran uses no rerun budget (Theseus review.yml uploads retry state only after finalize succeeds). Remaining for both Theseus items: BenchBox lock on v0.2.14, which is #4333 (another session's promotion PR, open). Close both when #4333 merges.
description:
On 2026-11-12 the `verdict / review` job for PR #4170 (run 43239267451) failed after 10 seconds in the step 'Prepare the review': `theseus_reviewer.github.GitHubError: gh api repos/BenchBox-dev/benchbox/pulls/4170 failed: gh: HTTP 503`. No reviewer ran, no verdict was posted, the `verdict posting check` and `review-gate` then failed, and the pull request stayed blocked until the review was dispatched again by hand with `gh workflow run review-verdict.yml --ref develop -f pr=4170 -f head=<sha>`. The failing code is in the pinned Theseus reviewer package, not in this repository.

Related: theseus-gate-transient-github-timeout-20261113 covers the same weakness in the gate's reads and states that `theseus_reviewer/github.py` already has a retry and backoff path. The failure here was raised from that module (`_gh_bytes`), so either that path does not cover this read or the 503 outlasted it.

Decision gate: establish first which of those is true, from the Theseus source at the pinned version. If one upstream change can fix both items, do it once and close both against the same Theseus release. The fix belongs upstream in Theseus; this item tracks the report and the pin that picks it up. Also decide whether a prepare-step failure should count against the daily rerun budget.

Guardrails.
- A failed or absent review is never worked around with a stand-in approval, a skipped check or a relaxed gate; the only recovery is to dispatch the review again for the same head.
- A Theseus lock change lands on its own pull request and is never part of a batch.
- A retry must apply only to idempotent reads; it must not repeat a post of a verdict or status.
